anthropic:agents:Agent.description:
A Claude Managed Agents agent: the model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and skills that sessions run with.

Agents are versioned. Every update that changes the configuration creates a new version, reported by the `version` output; sessions and deployments can pin a version, which makes canary and staged rollouts a matter of which version each deployment references.

The API cannot delete agents, so deleting this resource archives the agent, which makes it read-only. Running sessions continue; new sessions cannot use it.

createdAt.description: When the agent was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the agent, up to 2,048 characters.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the agent can connect to, up to 20. Each must be referenced by an `mcp_toolset` tool.

model.description: The model the agent runs on.

multiagent.description: Makes the agent a coordinator that delegates to other agents.

skills.description: The skills available to the agent.

system.description: The system prompt, up to 100,000 characters.

tools.description: The tools the agent can use, up to 128.

updatedAt.description: When the agent was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

version.description: The agent's current version. It starts at 1 and increments with every update that changes the configuration.

description.description: A description of the agent, up to 2,048 characters.

mcpServers.description: The MCP servers the agent can connect to, up to 20. Each must be referenced by an `mcp_toolset` tool.

model.description: The model the agent runs on.

multiagent.description: Makes the agent a coordinator that delegates to other agents.

skills.description: The skills available to the agent.

system.description: The system prompt, up to 100,000 characters.

tools.description: The tools the agent can use, up to 128.

anthropic:agents:Deployment.description:
A Claude Managed Agents deployment: an agent, an environment, and the events that start each session, run on a cron schedule or on demand.

A deployment runs one version of its agent. Set `agent.version` to the agent's `version` output to roll the deployment forward with every change to the agent, or to a fixed number to hold it back: updating the agent creates a new version, and deployments move to it one at a time as their `agent.version` changes.

The API cannot delete deployments, so deleting this resource archives the deployment, which stops its schedule and cannot be undone.

agent.description: The agent to run, and optionally the version to pin.

budget.description: A spending limit for the deployment.

createdAt.description: When the deployment was created, in RFC 3339 format.

initialEvents.description: The events that start each session, 1 to 50, in the API's event format. For example: `{type: "user.message", content: [{type: "text", text: "Triage new issues."}]}`.

paused.description: Whether the deployment is paused. Omit to leave pausing to other tools.

resources.description: Repositories, files, and memory stores mounted into each session, up to 500.

schedule.description: When to run. Omit to run only on demand.

status.description: Whether the deployment is `active` or `paused`. The platform also pauses a deployment when it cannot run, for example because its agent was archived.

updatedAt.description: When the deployment was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

vaultIds.description: Vaults whose credentials sessions can use, up to 50.

agent.description: The agent to run, and optionally the version to pin.

budget.description: A spending limit for the deployment.

anthropic:agents:Environment.description:
A Claude Managed Agents environment: where sessions run, either an Anthropic-managed cloud sandbox or a sandbox you host yourself.

Environments are not versioned; updates apply in place, and changing `config.type` replaces the environment. Deleting this resource deletes the environment. The API refuses to delete an environment that sessions still reference, in which case it is archived instead: it becomes read-only, running sessions continue, and new sessions cannot use it.

config.description: Where and how sessions run. Defaults to a cloud sandbox.

createdAt.description: When the environment was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the environment, up to 1,024 characters.

scope.description: Who can use the environment. API organizations accept only `organization`.

updatedAt.description: When the environment was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the environment, up to 1,024 characters.

scope.description: Who can use the environment. API organizations accept only `organization`.

anthropic:agents:MemoryStore.description:
A Claude Managed Agents memory store: persistent memory that agents read and write across sessions, attached to sessions or deployments as a resource. The memories themselves are data that agents write at runtime, so they are not managed here.

Deleting this resource deletes the store along with all of its memories and their versions.

createdAt.description: When the store was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: What the store holds, up to 1,024 characters. It is shown to the agent.

name.description: The store's name, 1 to 255 characters. It determines the path the store is mounted at in sessions, so renaming it moves the mount.

updatedAt.description: When the store was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: What the store holds, up to 1,024 characters. It is shown to the agent.

name.description: The store's name, 1 to 255 characters. It determines the path the store is mounted at in sessions, so renaming it moves the mount.

anthropic:agents:Tunnel.description:
An MCP tunnel, a research preview: a connection through which Managed Agents reach MCP servers on a private network, without exposing them to the internet. Run the tunnel client on the private network with the `tunnelToken` output, and trust its certificate authority with `TunnelCertificate`.

Tunnels cannot be updated, so changing the display name replaces the tunnel, which assigns a new domain and token. Deleting this resource archives the tunnel, which invalidates its token and archives its certificates; it cannot be undone.

createdAt.description: When the tunnel was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The tunnel's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

domain.description: The tunnel's globally unique domain, which MCP server URLs use.

tunnelToken.description: The token the tunnel client authenticates with.

displayName.description: The tunnel's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

anthropic:agents:TunnelCertificate.description:
A CA certificate for an MCP tunnel, used to verify the certificates of MCP servers behind the tunnel. A tunnel holds at most two active certificates, which allows rotation.

Certificates cannot be updated, so any change replaces the certificate. Deleting this resource archives the certificate. Its ID is `<tunnelId>/<certificateId>`.

caCertificatePem.description: A single PEM-encoded CA certificate, up to 8,192 characters.

createdAt.description: When the certificate was added, in RFC 3339 format.

expiresAt.description: When the certificate expires, in RFC 3339 format.

tunnelId.description: The tunnel that trusts the certificate.

caCertificatePem.description: A single PEM-encoded CA certificate, up to 8,192 characters.

tunnelId.description: The tunnel that trusts the certificate.

anthropic:agents:UserProfile.description:
A user profile: an entity your platform serves through the Anthropic API, such as an end user of your product or a company you resell Claude access to. Send its ID in the `anthropic-user-profile-id` header of Messages, Message Batches, and token counting requests to attribute them to the entity.

The API cannot delete user profiles, so deleting this resource only removes it from the stack; the profile remains.

accessType.description: How your platform uses the API on the entity's behalf. Defaults to `application`.

createdAt.description: When the profile was created, in RFC 3339 format.

externalId.description: Your platform's own identifier for the entity, up to 255 characters.

externalUserOnboardedAt.description: When the entity joined your platform, in RFC 3339 format. Once set, it cannot be cleared.

trustGrants.description: The profile's active or pending trust grants, by grant name.

updatedAt.description: When the profile was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

accessType.description: How your platform uses the API on the entity's behalf. Defaults to `application`.

externalId.description: Your platform's own identifier for the entity, up to 255 characters.

externalUserOnboardedAt.description: When the entity joined your platform, in RFC 3339 format. Once set, it cannot be cleared.

anthropic:agents:Vault.description:
A Claude Managed Agents vault: a container for the credentials sessions use to reach MCP servers and other services. Add credentials with `VaultCredential`, and attach vaults to sessions or deployments by ID.

Deleting this resource deletes the vault and every credential in it.

createdAt.description: When the vault was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The vault's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

updatedAt.description: When the vault was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: The vault's display name, 1 to 255 characters.

anthropic:agents:VaultCredential.description:
A credential in a Claude Managed Agents vault: an OAuth grant or bearer token for an MCP server, or a secret injected into outbound requests as an environment variable.

Secret values are write-only: the API never returns them, so changes made to them outside of Pulumi cannot be detected. Changing the credential's type, MCP server URL, secret name, or OAuth client or token endpoint replaces it; because these must be unique within a vault, the old credential is deleted before the new one is created. Its ID is `<vaultId>/<credentialId>`.

createdAt.description: When the credential was created, in RFC 3339 format.

updatedAt.description: When the credential was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

anthropic:identity:FederationIssuer.description:
A workload identity federation issuer: an OIDC identity provider, such as GitHub Actions, a Kubernetes cluster, or a cloud's workload identity service, whose signed tokens workloads exchange for short-lived Anthropic access tokens. Which tokens are accepted, and which service account they act as, is decided by `FederationRule`s.

Managing federation requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`).

The API cannot delete issuers, so deleting this resource archives the issuer. Archiving is refused while a live rule references the issuer.

checkJti.description: Whether to reject tokens whose `jti` claim has been seen before. Defaults to `true`.

createdAt.description: When the issuer was created, in RFC 3339 format.

issuerUrl.description: The issuer URL, which must match the `iss` claim of accepted tokens.

jwks.description: Where the issuer's signing keys come from. Defaults to OIDC discovery from the issuer URL.

maxJwtLifetimeSeconds.description: The longest lifetime, in seconds, a token may have to be accepted, between 1 and 176,400. Defaults to 3,600.

name.description: A lowercase slug that uniquely names the issuer in the organization, 1 to 255 characters.

pollStatus.description: The health of the platform's polling of the issuer's signing keys.

updatedAt.description: When the issuer was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

checkJti.description: Whether to reject tokens whose `jti` claim has been seen before. Defaults to `true`.

anthropic:identity:FederationRule.description:
A workload identity federation rule: tokens from an issuer that satisfy the rule's `match` are exchanged for access tokens that act as the rule's target service account, with the rule's OAuth scope.

A rule applies either to all workspaces (`appliesToAllWorkspaces`) or to the workspace it is created in (`workspaceId`); bind it to further workspaces with `FederationRuleWorkspace`.

Managing federation requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`).

The API cannot delete rules, so deleting this resource archives the rule.

appliesToAllWorkspaces.description: Whether the rule applies to every workspace. Otherwise `workspaceId` is required.

createdAt.description: When the rule was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the rule, up to 2,000 characters.

issuerId.description: The ID of the issuer whose tokens the rule accepts. Changing it replaces the rule.

issuerName.description: The name of the rule's issuer.

match.description: The conditions a token must satisfy. At least one of `subjectPrefix`, `claims`, or `condition` is required.

name.description: A lowercase slug that uniquely names the rule in the organization.

oauthScope.description: The space-separated OAuth scopes of the access tokens the rule issues, such as `workspace:developer`.

target.description: The service account the rule's access tokens act as.

tokenLifetimeSeconds.description: The lifetime, in seconds, of the access tokens the rule issues, between 60 and 86,400. Defaults to 3,600.

updatedAt.description: When the rule was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the rule is created in, required unless `appliesToAllWorkspaces` is set. Changing it replaces the rule; to bind the rule to further workspaces, use `FederationRuleWorkspace`.

workspaceIds.description: Every workspace the rule is bound to.

anthropic:identity:FederationRuleWorkspa.description:
Binds a federation rule to a workspace, so that the rule's access tokens can act in it. The resource's ID is `<federation-rule-id>/<workspace-id>`.

Do not also bind the workspace the rule was created in (its `workspaceId`): that binding belongs to the rule.

Managing federation requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`).

createdAt.description: When the binding was created, in RFC 3339 format.

workspaceName.description: The workspace's name when the binding was created.

anthropic:identity:RbacGroup.description:
A role-based access control group of users. Add users with `RbacGroupMember`. Roles are attached to groups in the organization's admin settings, and are reported by `roleIds`.

RBAC groups are available to Claude Enterprise organizations. Groups provisioned by SCIM cannot be changed or deleted while SCIM provisioning is active.

createdAt.description: When the group was created, in RFC 3339 format.

name.description: The group's name, 1 to 255 characters. Names need not be unique.

roleIds.description: The IDs of the roles attached to the group.

sourceType.description: How the group was provisioned: `direct` or `scim`.

updatedAt.description: When the group was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

name.description: The group's name, 1 to 255 characters. Names need not be unique.

anthropic:identity:RbacGroupMember.description:
Adds a user to an RBAC group. The resource's ID is `<rbac-group-id>/<user-id>`.

RBAC groups are available to Claude Enterprise organizations.

createdAt.description: When the user was added to the group, in RFC 3339 format.

anthropic:identity:ServiceAccount.description:
A service account: a non-human identity that workloads assume through workload identity federation (see `FederationRule`), in place of long-lived API keys. Grant it access to workspaces with `ServiceAccountWorkspace`.

Managing service accounts requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`); the API does not accept Admin API keys for them.

The API cannot delete service accounts, so deleting this resource archives it. Archiving is refused while a live federation rule targets the account.

createdAt.description: When the service account was created, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the service account, up to 2,000 characters.

name.description: A slug that uniquely names the service account in the organization. It cannot be changed; changing it replaces the service account.

organizationRole.description: The service account's organization role. Defaults to `developer`.

updatedAt.description: When the service account was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

description.description: A description of the service account, up to 2,000 characters.

name.description: A slug that uniquely names the service account in the organization. It cannot be changed; changing it replaces the service account.

organizationRole.description: The service account's organization role. Defaults to `developer`.

anthropic:identity:ServiceAccountWorkspa.description:
Grants a service account a role in a workspace. The resource's ID is `<workspace-id>/<service-account-id>`.

Every service account is implicitly a `workspace_user` of the organization's default workspace; that membership cannot be removed, so do not manage it with this resource.

Managing service accounts requires an OAuth token with the `org:admin` scope (`anthropic:authToken`).

workspaceRole.description: The service account's role in the workspace.
The service account's role in the workspace.

anthropic:organization:ApiKey.description:
An API key's name and status.

API keys cannot be created through the API, only in the Claude Console, and their secret values are never returned. Creating this resource adopts an existing key by ID; fields left undeclared are left as they are.

Deleting this resource archives the key, which permanently revokes it. To stop managing a key without revoking it, set the `retainOnDelete` resource option.

apiKeyId.description: The ID of the existing API key to manage.

createdAt.description: When the key was created, in RFC 3339 format.

expiresAt.description: When the key expires, in RFC 3339 format, if it does.

partialKeyHint.description: A redacted hint of the key's value, for recognizing it.

status.description: The key's status. An archived key cannot be reactivated.

workspaceId.description: The ID of the workspace the key belongs to.

apiKeyId.description: The ID of the existing API key to manage.

status.description: The key's status. An archived key cannot be reactivated.

anthropic:organization:ComplianceSetting.description:
The organization's compliance settings, which control the Compliance API. An organization has exactly one set, so declare at most one of these per organization.

An organization with a parent inherits its parent's settings, and provisioning Access Transparency re-enables the Compliance API, which a refresh reports as drift.

Settings cannot be deleted, so deleting this resource leaves them as they are.

enabled.description: Whether the Compliance API is enabled.
Whether the Compliance API is enabled.

anthropic:organization:Invite.description: An invitation to join the organization. Invitations cannot be changed, so any change replaces the invitation, and they expire 21 days after they are sent. Once accepted, the person is a user of the organization; manage their role with `anthropic.organization.User`.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation expires, in RFC 3339 format.

invitedAt.description: When the invitation was sent, in RFC 3339 format.

rbacGroupIds.description: The RBAC groups the person joins. Claude Enterprise only.

role.description: The organization role the person joins with.

rbacGroupIds.description: The RBAC groups the person joins. Claude Enterprise only.

role.description: The organization role the person joins with.

anthropic:organization:SpendLimit.description:
A spend limit: the most a user, a workspace, or the whole organization may spend in a period.

There is at most one limit per scope and period, and the API sets a limit by overwriting whatever limit that scope and period already has, so creating this resource takes over an existing limit rather than failing. Changing the scope or period replaces the limit.

User limits apply to Claude Enterprise organizations. Organization and workspace limits for Console organizations are in early-access preview, and must be monthly with an amount.

amount.description: The limit, as a non-negative integer string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency: `"50000"` is $500.00. Omit for an explicit "no limit" override of this scope and period.

createdAt.description: When the limit was created, in RFC 3339 format.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the organization's billing currency, which `amount` is denominated in.

period.description: The period the limit applies over. If omitted, the API's default applies.

updatedAt.description: When the limit was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

amount.description: The limit, as a non-negative integer string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency: `"50000"` is $500.00. Omit for an explicit "no limit" override of this scope and period.

period.description: The period the limit applies over. If omitted, the API's default applies.

anthropic:organization:User.description:
A user of the organization, and their organization role.

Users cannot be created through the API: people join by accepting an `anthropic.organization.Invite`. Creating this resource adopts an existing user by ID and sets their role.

Deleting this resource removes the user from the organization. To stop managing a user without removing them, set the `retainOnDelete` resource option.

addedAt.description: When the user joined the organization, in RFC 3339 format.

role.description: The user's organization role. The `admin` role cannot be granted through the API.

userId.description: The ID of the existing user to manage.

role.description: The user's organization role. The `admin` role cannot be granted through the API.

userId.description: The ID of the existing user to manage.

anthropic:organization:Workspace.description:
A workspace: a unit of isolation for API keys, usage, limits, and workspace-scoped resources such as agents and skills.

The API cannot delete workspaces, so deleting this resource archives the workspace, which cannot be undone.

compartmentId.description: The ID of the storage compartment that holds the workspace's data.

createdAt.description: When the workspace was created, in RFC 3339 format.

dataResidency.description: Where the workspace's data is stored and where inference may run.

displayColor.description: The color the Console shows the workspace in, as `#RRGGBB`.

externalKeyId.description: The ID of a customer-managed encryption key (an `anthropic.security.ExternalKey`) that encrypts the workspace's data. It can be set on a workspace that has none, but once set it can never be changed or removed, so any change to it replaces the workspace.

tags.description: Tags for the workspace. Keys may not start with `anthropic`.

dataResidency.description: Where the workspace's data is stored and where inference may run.

displayColor.description: The color the Console shows the workspace in, as `#RRGGBB`.

externalKeyId.description: The ID of a customer-managed encryption key (an `anthropic.security.ExternalKey`) that encrypts the workspace's data. It can be set on a workspace that has none, but once set it can never be changed or removed, so any change to it replaces the workspace.

tags.description: Tags for the workspace. Keys may not start with `anthropic`.

anthropic:organization:WorkspaceMember.description: A user's membership of a workspace, with a workspace role. The user must already be a member of the organization. The resource's ID is `<workspaceId>/<userId>`.

workspaceRole.description: The user's role in the workspace.
The user's role in the workspace.

anthropic:security:ExternalKey.description:
A customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) held in AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault. A workspace encrypts its data with the key once the workspace's `externalKeyId` refers to it.

Creating the key validates it with a round trip to the KMS, and fails, leaving nothing behind, if Anthropic cannot use it. The key's provider configuration and geography cannot change once a workspace uses the key, so changing either replaces the key.

Deleting the key is refused while a workspace uses it.

attachment.description: Whether a workspace uses the key: `attached` or `unattached`.

createdAt.description: When the key was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A display name for the key, 1 to 255 characters.

geo.description: The geography the key serves. The only accepted value is `us`.

updatedAt.description: When the key was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A display name for the key, 1 to 255 characters.

geo.description: The geography the key serves. The only accepted value is `us`.

anthropic:skills:Skill.description:
A custom Agent Skill: a directory of instructions, scripts, and resources, with a `SKILL.md` at its root, that Claude loads when relevant. Skills can be attached to Managed Agents and used from the Messages API.

Skills are versioned. When the content of `source` changes, a new immutable version is uploaded and becomes `latestVersionId`; earlier versions are kept, so agents that pin one keep working. Deleting the resource deletes the skill and all of its versions.

createdAt.description: When the skill was created, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A human-readable label for the skill, up to 255 characters. Defaults to the `name` in the `SKILL.md` frontmatter. The API cannot rename a skill, so changing this replaces it.

latestVersionId.description: The ID of the newest version (`skver_...`), which agents can pin in a skill reference's `version`.

source.description: The skill's files, such as a `FileArchive` of the skill's directory. `SKILL.md` must sit at the root of the archive, or at the root of its single top-level directory. Up to 30 MB uncompressed.

updatedAt.description: When the skill was last updated, in RFC 3339 format.

displayName.description: A human-readable label for the skill, up to 255 characters. Defaults to the `name` in the `SKILL.md` frontmatter. The API cannot rename a skill, so changing this replaces it.

source.description: The skill's files, such as a `FileArchive` of the skill's directory. `SKILL.md` must sit at the root of the archive, or at the root of its single top-level directory. Up to 30 MB uncompressed.

anthropic:index:getModels.description: Lists the Claude models available to the provider's workspace, newest first.

anthropic:index:getOrganization.description: Reads the organization that the provider's Admin API key or OAuth token belongs to.

anthropic:index:getRateLimits.description: Reads the rate limits that apply to the organization or, given a `workspaceId`, to one workspace. Rate limits are set by Anthropic and cannot be managed through the API.

workspaceId.description: The workspace to read limits for. Omit for the organization's limits.

rateLimits.description: The rate limits, one entry per group of models or API feature.
